newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Khumalo forms new 3 bln rand mine firm.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Khumalo forms new 3 bln rand mine firm.

text.p: South African businessman Mzi Khumalo, chairman of JCI Ltd, said on Tuesday he was forming a new three billion rand black-controlled mining holding company.

The move follows the acquisition of control of Witwatersrand Nigel (Pty) Ltd by Khumalo's African Mining Group and the reversal of Khumalo Holdings and the entire issued share capital of Consolidated Mining Corp Ltd into property loan stock company NK Properties Ltd.
As a result, NKP will hold a 34.9 percent shareholding in Saflife Ltd. Along with other black shareholders, this will result in 55 percent of Saflife being held by black empowerment groups.

In the first leg of the deal CMC, controlled by the Kebble family, will be reversed into NKP, of which the Khumalo Consortium becomes the ultimate controlling shareholder. NKP will acquire an additional 28.4 million Saflife shares as well as shareholdings in JCI and Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd.
NKP will be renamed and listed under the "Mining Holdings" sector on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, with CMC's Brett Kebble as chief executive and Khumalo as chairman.
Khumalo said the company would seek to increase shareholder value by focusing on undervalued mining companies through acquisitions, mergers and break-ups.
"We will invest in mining assets as a major shareholder but not as an operator," he said in a statement.
He added that the deal did not hinge on a possible merger between JCI and Lonrho Plc.

Following the implementation of the acquisitions, NKP will have a direct holding in JCI of six percent and WitNigel will have an option to purchase a further 4.9 percent of JCI, which in addition to Saflife's holdings of 30 percent, will result in these black-controlled groups holdings a very significant stake in JCI.
